newsitem.title: USA: Asarco's profits plunge along with copper prices.
newsitem.headline: Asarco's profits plunge along with copper prices.

text.p: Asarco Inc. said Thursday that its profits nose-dived to one-tenth of what they were a year ago as lower prices for most metals, especially copper, reduced its sales by 20 percent.
The New York-based mining company said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 plunged to $6.0 million, or 14 cents a share, from $58.3 million, or $1.38 per common share.
It said lower prices -- especially for copper, which is still reeling from the trading scandal at Sumitomo Corp. -- sent its sales plummeting by 20.9 percent to $647.8 million from $819.7 million.
"Asarco's earnings for the third quarter reflect the sharp decline in copper prices from the prior year," Chairman Richard Osborne said in a statement.
"The decline in the copper price between this year and last is estimated to have reduced the company's net earnings by approximately $67 million in the third quarter."

The company said lower metal prices also significantly reduced its sales and profits for the first nine months of the year. It said net income fell to $114.0 million, or $2.67 a share, from $180.4 million, or $4.27 a share, as sales slipped to $2.05 billion from $2.40 billion.
Asarco said the average price of copper on metals exchanges in New York and London in the quarter were one-third of what they were a year ago.
It also said the average price of silver, lead and molybdenum were lower in the latest quarter while zinc prices were just slightly higher.
"The (copper) market is not yet free from the uncertainties created by the trading losses of one large market participant," Osborne said in his statement.
The company said results from its other business segments, speciality chemicals and aggregates, continued to be good.
It said the aggregates segment posted a 12.5 percent increase in sales as a result of strong construction business in its area of operations.
Asarco's stock lost 37.5 cents to $26 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
